subject: Clarify: Do you train on customer data? + deletion/retention specifics
messages:
From: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@finserve.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: legal@finserve.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Q on training and retention (FinServe)

Hi Jasmine,

Quick one from our security/legal review: does Redwood ever use customer request/response data to train or update models? We have a strict policy about data not being used for model training unless explicitly contracted. Also can you confirm typical retention windows for request logs, KV cache, and backups, and what the deletion process looks like (and how long backups persist after a deletion request)?

We need something we can show our InfoSec team and optionally incorporate into a DPA amendment. If you have a short summary PDF that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Carlos Ramirez
Head of Engineering, FinServe Corp

--
FinServe Corp

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@finserve.com>
Cc: legal@finserve.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, priya.natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q on training and retention (FinServe)

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear question. Short answer: by default Redwood does NOT train customer-specific models on customer request or response payloads. Below I summarized the practical guarantees and operational nuances so your InfoSec and legal teams can see the specifics. I attached a short Data_Handling_Summary.pdf with the same points.

1) "No training" guarantee
- Hosted API: Redwood’s default policy is that we do not use customer-provided prompt / response content to update weights or fine-tune models. We may use aggregated telemetry (latency, error rates, token distribution) for safety and product improvements, but that telemetry is aggregated and cannot be traced back to a single customer.
- Dedicated & Private deployments: For Dedicated capacity the customer can opt into metric reporting only; model updates are not performed using tenant data. For Private (VPC / on-prem) customers, all model artifacts and inference are under customer control; Redwood does not access or use inference payloads for model training.

2) Retention windows (typical)
- Request logs (text payloads): Hosted default retention is 30 days for operational debugging. This is configurable and can be reduced via contract (we support 0d / 7d / 30d options).
- KV cache & in-memory session state: Ephemeral by design; persisted KV caches exist only when explicitly enabled for session continuity and are retained per configured TTL (default 0–24 hours).
- Backups / disaster recovery snapshots: Backups of system metadata (not user text payloads) are retained for up to 90 days; if a customer requests deletion we initiate retention purging but backups may persist until the next overwrite/retention cycle. For high-assurance commitments we offer a contractual shorter backup retention or private deployment.

3) Deletion process
- Self-service: Customers can delete data via Console/API (delete keys, clear sessions).
- Escalated/manual: For legal or compliance requests we provide a verified deletion flow: submit request, engineering performs purge across active stores, and we certify completion within the contracted SLA window (commonly 30 days unless otherwise negotiated).
- Backups & archive: We include a statement in the DPA describing backup retention behavior and an expected timeline for purge from backups (e.g., up to N days depending on backup cadence).

4) Proof and auditability
- Customers on Dedicated/Private get audit logs and can integrate their KMS/HSM.
- We provide SOC 2 controls mapping and can include deletion confirmations and timestamps in the audit log exports for Enterprise contracts.

5) Exceptions & opt-in training
- We will never train models on customer data without explicit, written opt-in (separate contract). Any training work would be scoped, timeboxed, and auditable.

Next steps
- I attached a one-page Data_Handling_Summary.pdf for your InfoSec. If you want contractual language we can propose DPA draft text; Marcus (cc'd) can confirm the legal commitment level we can offer in Standard vs. Enterprise terms.

If helpful, we can run a short session with your InfoSec to walk through telemetry examples and the audit evidence we can provide.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Data_Handling_Summary.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Thanks Jasmine — adding one note from a contract perspective: we can commit to the "no training without explicit opt-in" clause in the DPA for Enterprise customers. For Hosted customers we include the standard operational retention terms (30d request logs, backup policy) and an option to purchase a reduced-retention add-on or move to Dedicated/Private.

Carlos — happy to have our legal team draft a short DPA amendment that inserts the 0d/7d/30d selectable retention windows and a deletion certification clause. I dropped a draft in the shared Drive link (see link in the thread).

—Marcus
VP, Legal Operations — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the detailed response and the PDF, Jasmine — that helps. Our legal team reviewed and has two asks: 1) can Redwood guarantee a 30-day max for deletion certification (i.e., full purge from active stores and confirmation), and 2) can you provide a single-point summary we can add to our procurement checklist stating "Redwood does not use customer submission data to train models without explicit opt-in" with a reference to DPA section once signed?

Also: we would like the DPA to include explicit language about backups being deleted within 60 days of a deletion request. Is that something you can offer for an Enterprise contract?

If you can send a DPA draft and a brief note we can attach to our procurement record, we can move this forward.

Cheers,
Carlos

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Carlos — great, appreciate the clarity. Confirming next steps and commitments we can operationalize for an Enterprise contract: 

- Deletion certification SLA: Redwood will certify purge from active stores within 30 calendar days of a validated deletion request. (We will include evidence: timestamps and audit log excerpts.)
- Backup retention SLA: For Enterprise customers we can contractually commit to purge customer-related backups within 60 calendar days (subject to agreed backup cadence and region-specific constraints).
- DPA language: We will add the explicit statement you requested: "Redwood does not use customer submission data to train models without explicit opt-in and written agreement." We will circulate a DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Draft_v2.docx attached) with the above windows and the selectable retention options documented.

- I will upload the DPA draft and a one-page procurement-friendly summary to the shared drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleShareLink) by end of day Monday.
- Marcus will coordinate legal sign-off on the DPA language.
